title: Deep SPI: Safe Policy Improvement via World Models
claim: A large environment with many states can be abstracted into a small world model whose latent states preserve transition and reward structure.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, region blobs mapped to latent-state graph
description: Two side-by-side panels with a shared color code. Panel (a) shows a large MDP whose state space is split into four colored blob regions: S1 (lavender), S2 (light teal), S3 (pink) and S4 (light green). Curved arrows labeled a1, a2 and a3 link the regions. S1 leads to S2 via a1, S2 leads to S4 via a3, and S1 leads to S3 via a2. Panel (b) shows the matching abstract world model as a graph of circular latent states s̄1, s̄2, s̄3, s̄3′ and s̄4. Each circle has the color of its region. Edges carry transition probabilities such as 4/5, 1/5, 3/4, 1/4, 9/10 and 1/10. Self-loops are drawn on several nodes. Green reward labels (+1 on s̄4, +20 between s̄3 and s̄3′) mark the rewards. The eye goes first to the colored blobs on the left, then to the graph on the right. Captions with math notation sit under each panel.
caption: In M, continuously playing a1 in states from S1 eventually leads the agent to the region S2, and playing a3 in S2 eventually leads the agent to S4 where a reward of 1 is incurred at each time step, whatever the action played. Playing a2 in S1 leads the agent to the region S3, where all actions incur negative rewards. Here, ϕ(s) = ¯si for any s ∈Si and i = {1, 2, 4}. For s ∈S3, we have either ϕ(s) = ¯s3 or ϕ(s) = ¯s′
abstract: Safe policy improvement (SPI) offers theoretical control over policy updates, yet existing guarantees largely concern offline, tabular reinforcement learning (RL). We study SPI in general online settings, when combined with world model and representation learning. We develop a theoretical framework showing that restricting policy updates to a well-defined neighborhood of the current policy ensures monotonic improvement and convergence. This analysis links transition and reward prediction losses to representation quality, yielding online, "deep" analogues of classical SPI theorems from the offline RL literature. Building on these results, we introduce DeepSPI, a principled on-policy algorithm that couples local transition and reward losses with regularised policy updates. On the ALE-57 benchmark, DeepSPI matches or exceeds strong baselines, including PPO and DeepMDPs, while retaining theoretical guarantees.
